title: Learning from Comparison: Constrained Projection Policy Optimization for Pareto-Front Improvement
claim: A learning loop turns sampled-group evaluations into feasibility- and progress-aware comparisons, which drive a constrained projection that updates the policy.

description: A block-diagram loop. The top row runs left to right: grey Context, blue Policy Model, orange Evaluation (Simulation), then a large green rounded panel titled Objective-Induced Comparisons. A dashed arrow runs down from Evaluation to a grey Feasible PF achieve box and then into the panel. The panel holds four small insets. A is a 2-D f1/f2 Pareto-front scatter with feasible and infeasible points. B shows progress toward the front, labeled as PF progress. C shows a feasible/infeasible split labeled v=0. abstract: Constrained multi-objective reinforcement learning aims to discover a diverse set of feasible trade-offs, yet scalarization and signed, normalized group-relative advantages can be brittle under objective-scale drift, near-ties, and feasibility scarcity. We propose constrained projection policy optimization (CoPro), which alternates between an E-step moment projection and an M-step policy projection. In the E-step, we solve a Kullback-Leibler (KL)-regularized, moment-constrained projection over each sampled group to compute a nonnegative reweighting distribution ($ q^* $) that promotes feasible Pareto-front (PF) progress, preserves feasibility anchors, and suppresses ambiguous near-ties. This E-step admits a closed-form exponential-family solution and guarantees strictly positive probability mass on feasible anchors whenever feasible candidates appear in the group. In the M-step, we project the policy toward $ q^* $ via weighted maximum likelihood with a trust-region regularizer, yielding a PF-aligned update direction from comparisons without hand-crafted reward shaping. Empirically, CoPro improves feasible PF quality and robustness on constrained multi-objective benchmarks for large language model tool use and analog circuit design tasks; code is available at \href{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/CoPro-8A95/README.md}{\texttt{CoPro}}.
